text:
sec-oncall: Alert: noticed a huge S3 upload at 2026-03-19T02:12:06Z from the analytics pipeline. ~12GB CSV, ~1.2M rows. Not in today's deploy notes. :eyes:

jake: where did it land? prefix?

sec-oncall: s3://redwood-exports/prod/one-off/2026-03-19/analytics-dump-20260319.csv.gz

infra-bot: [alert] s3 upload 12.3GB by service_account:analytics-runner@redwood-prod at 2026-03-19T02:12:06Z (kms:cust-key-redwood-prod)

maya: that SA is the scheduled nightly job runner. Did we have a schedule change?

samir: checking scheduler — no cron changes in the last 72h. listing recent jobs...

data-platform: log snippet: 
```
BigQuery job  jobId=projects/redwood/jobs/abc123 finished. query: EXPORT DATA OPTIONS(uri='s3://redwood-exports/prod/one-off/analytics-dump-20260319.csv.gz', format='CSV') AS SELECT * FROM prod.user_events WHERE event_time < '2026-03-19';
```

olivia: EXPORT DATA was used, not a custom CSV script. That indicates someone ran a BigQuery export job (or a job that calls export API).

alice: audit logs show identity: serviceAccount:analytics-runner@redwood-prod oauth client: api-key-xxxxxx. IAM shows analytics-runner has roles/bigquery.jobUser and roles/storage.objectCreator on redwood-exports prefix since last month (requested during onboarding).

jake: any evidence of exfil to an external account? ACLs on bucket?

sec-oncall: bucket policy: public=false, ACLs default. Object ACL for that object: owner=redwood-svc, grantee=redwood-analytics-group only. No public ACLs.

samir: KMS logs show decrypt/wrap with customer key cust-key-redwood-prod used at the time of upload. Principal: analytics-runner@redwood-prod had kms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToEncrypt permission via role binding added 2026-02-14 (infra change).

maya: so principal had permissions and the bucket only allowed internal write. Do we treat this as suspicious? Could be an expected large export. But no one claims it.

olivia: I paged the analytics on-call. They confirm no scheduled ad-hoc export and no one initiated a manual export at that time.

jake: immediate containment: 1) revoke analytics-runner write access to the S3 prefix, 2) disable the service account keys/token, 3) snapshot the object and isolate it to a quarantine bucket with restricted access for forensics.

sec-oncall: executing containment steps now. 
- iam: removed storage.objectCreator on prefix (applied)
- service account: disabled impulse tokens created in last 48h (revoked)
- moved object to s3://redwood-exports-quarantine/prod/one-off/analytics-dump-20260319.csv.gz (copy preserved, original deleted)

infra-bot: action log: iam change by sec-oncall at 2026-03-19T02:45:02Z, sa tokens revoked by sec-oncall at 2026-03-19T02:47:10Z, object moved by infra-bot at 2026-03-19T02:50:33Z

samir: can we inspect the CSV headers to see which tables/columns were exported? Any PII columns?

sec-oncall: forensic snapshot: first rows show columns: user_id,email_masked,ip_country,event_type,event_timestamp,payload_summary. email_masked shows hashed emails, not plaintext. user_id = internal UUIDs. No SSNs, no payment PANs observed in sample.

maya: that's a relief but we need a full scan. Run quick grep for patterns that look like full emails or CC numbers.

data-platform: ran grep on the snapshot for regex patterns of 16-digit numbers and full emails. Results: 0 matches for 16-digit PANs, ~30 matches for plain emails (looks like a few rows that didn't have proper masking). Timestamps and event payloads consistent with analytics events.

olivia: where did the export job originate? Trace the BigQuery job user agent and submitter.

alice: BigQuery audit shows jobUser: analytics-runner@redwood-prod andRequesterEmail: pipeline-orchestrator@redwood-prod (the airflow account). Job submitted via airflow task id: export_user_events_20260319. Task log: `trigger_export('2026-03-19')` at 02:11:40Z.

jake: check airflow run: was it triggered by scheduler or via REST?

samir: airflow logs show a manual trigger via web UI from IP 52.12.34.56 at 02:10Z. User: cn=harper@redwood.com (internal). Harper on analytics team.

olivia: pinging @harper offline — she replied: "I launched a test export to validate revised column mapping. I thought it would write to staging, not prod. My bad."

maya: ok so root cause = human operator error + misconfigured export target. Why did UI allow prod target? Did RBAC prevent production exports from non-prod contexts?

alice: RBAC note: we rely on SA roles and bucket policies. The workflow allowed the web UI user to trigger a task that uses analytics-runner SA which has write access. No extra guard.

sec-oncall: classification: accidental data exposure risk, low-severity because bucket internal and most PII masked, but policy violation and some unmasked emails present. Recommend we treat as incident and run post-incident actions.

jake: recommended immediate remediation items: 1) add guarded export validation that prevents prod target exports from web UI unless dual-approval, 2) tighten SA permissions so that the pipeline must assume scoped tokens that are environment-limited, 3) rotate any credentials that may be affected, 4) remediate unmasked emails by re-masking source data.

samir: also recommend KMS key policy change: disallow direct key use from analytics-runner principal for new encrypt ops; only allow encryption via a service that enforces export labels. Create a restricted wrapper that checks dest bucket and mask state before allowing encrypt.

olivia: will take ownership of the dual-approval UI guard and add a feature flag. ETA 2d. 

maya: I'll own RBAC hardening and short-lived scoped tokens for pipelines. ETA 3d to roll a policy and prod deploy.

alice: I'll re-run the data scan and prepare a list of affected rows (the ~30 non-masked emails). Work with privacy to notify if needed. ETA today EOD.

sec-oncall: created ticket ENGSEC-3241 and linked to tasks. Communication plan: no external notification required at this time, internal incident report to be shared with legal and privacy.

olivia: question for infra: can we add a KMS audit trigger that alerts on any encrypt/decrypt from this key where the destination bucket is prod and the calling principal is analytics-runner?

infra-bot: suggestion: we can create a Cloud Audit Log sink + Cloud Function that filters: protoPayload.methodName:"Encrypt" OR "AsymmetricEncrypt" AND resourceName: "cust-key-redwood-prod" AND protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail:"analytics-runner@redwood-prod" AND protoPayload.resourceName contains "redwood-exports/prod" -> send to PagerDuty. Feasible.

jake: good. let's implement that. Assign infra to set up alert.

samir: postmortem: schedule 72h review with analytics, infra, security, and privacy; document timeline, root cause, actions completed, and closure criteria.

sec-oncall: incident status: contained, forensic snapshot taken, low PII impact, mitigation tasks assigned. Closing task list and will post the incident summary in #incidents after the postmortem. :lock:

olivia: added follow-up: update runbooks to include a pre-export destination check and KMS policy checklist.

alice: uploading full evidence bundle to secure evidence store (ticket ENGSEC-3241).

jake: thanks all. If anyone finds additional exports in the last 7 days, ping this thread.

sec-oncall: thread closed for now. Postmortem scheduled 2026-03-22 15:00 UTC.
